biggest_catch: A straightforward $200 for $500 of planned spending, with no annual fee. Year-one math: $200 bonus minus the $0 annual fee leaves $200 net in the first year. Only claim this if you were already going to spend that $500 on normal purchases; never spend extra to hit the target. Freedom products are generally unavailable to anyone who currently holds that Freedom product or received its new-cardmember bonus in the previous 24 months, and Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern still applies.
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $500 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: $200 cash back minus the $0 annual fee leaves $200 net in the first year. From year two there is no fee and no bonus, so the card only keeps paying you through its normal 5% travel, 3% dining and drugstores, and 1.5% everything-else cash back.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.

The bonus is generally unavailable if you currently hold this Freedom product or received its new-cardmember bonus in the previous 24 months. Check the current application terms if you had a Freedom Unlimited or the older Freedom card recently.
Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit.
The account must be open and not in default when the bonus is paid, and the bonus is paid only once per account.

steps: Go to the official Chase Freedom page and read the current offer headline and the Pricing & Terms before anything else.
Confirm your eligibility: you do not currently hold the Freedom product and have not received its new-cardmember bonus in the previous 24 months.
Apply online. Expect a hard credit inquiry.
Use the card for the purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $500 in the first 3 months from account opening.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met for the $200 bonus to post, and confirm it appears as Ultimate Rewards cash back.
Keep using the card for its 1.5% unlimited cash back (and 5%/3% category rates) if that fits your normal spending; there is no fee either way.
timing: Spend $500 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Bonus posts after qualifying purchases, typically 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met.
